City council approves new cycle lanes across the old town

By A. Reporter · Updated 30 Oct 2026, 9:14 am

The city council on Thursday approved a plan to build twelve kilometres of protected cycle lanes through the old town, ending a debate that has run for more than two years.

ADVERTISEMENT

Under the plan, the lanes will be separated from traffic by a low kerb, and three junctions near the market will be redesigned so that cyclists get their own signal phase.

Shopkeepers on Market Road had opposed an earlier version that removed most street parking. The approved version keeps about half of the spaces and adds loading bays at either end of the street.

What happens next

Work on the first section, between the railway station and the river, is expected to start in January and take about four months. The council said the remaining sections would follow through 2027.

"This is the most important change to the old town's streets in a generation," the mayor told reporters after the vote.

Residents can see the final drawings at the council office and on its website until the end of November, and can send comments on the junction designs during that period.
